scenes.title: Families of Noah’s sons

art.alt: Native text diagram of Noah’s sons and selected named descendants; not a map, timeline, or full genealogy.

scenes.caption: Diagram · Genesis 10:1–6, 21–22 · not geography, chronology, or a complete genealogy

intro.title: Selected families
intro.note: The branches show only names and relationships in the selected verses. They do not assign modern identities, boundaries, or dates.

hotspots.title: Noah and his sons
hotspots.note: The root and three son branches are visible in the diagram; the anchor is the passage that names the family.

hotspots.title: Japheth’s family
hotspots.note: The named sons of Japheth and selected Gomer/Javan descendants appear as text. The note for verse 5 avoids drawing borders or assigning modern peoples.

hotspots.title: Ham’s sons
hotspots.note: The four sons named in verse 6 are listed beneath Ham.

hotspots.title: Shem and his named children
hotspots.note: The diagram states the Eber-descendant relation in verse 21 separately and lists the children named in verse 22; it does not add intervening branches.

scenes.title: Names and a promised son
scenes.coverage: Genesis 17:5, 15, 19–21 · names and future promise only

art.alt: Text-only diagram linking Abram with Abraham, Sarai with Sarah, and identifying Isaac as promised for the future. No event or portrait.

scenes.caption: Diagram · Genesis 17:5, 15, 19–21 · not a map, timeline, birth scene, or full chapter

intro.title: Name changes and promise
intro.note: The passage gives new names and speaks of a future son; this diagram shows those textual links without picturing an event or implying the child is already born.

hotspots.title: Abram is named Abraham
hotspots.note: Both names and the name-giving reference are visible in the diagram.

hotspots.title: Sarai is named Sarah
hotspots.note: Both names and the name-giving reference are visible in the diagram.

hotspots.title: Isaac is promised to Sarah and Abraham
hotspots.note: Isaac is labeled as promised for the future, with the selected promise range. No birth scene is shown.

scenes.title: Family relationships and response

art.alt: Native text relationship guide showing Dinah as daughter of Jacob and Leah, Simeon and Levi as named brothers, and the closing exchange. No assault or retaliation is pictured.

scenes.caption: Relationship diagram · Genesis 34:1, 25, 30–31 · not a map, timeline, or full chapter; no assault or retaliation illustration

intro.title: Selected relationships
intro.note: The lines show only the family links named in the selected verses. The diagram addresses the chapter’s closing exchange without depicting or replacing its assault and retaliation.

hotspots.title: Dinah, daughter of Leah and Jacob
hotspots.note: The two parent links and Dinah’s name are visible; the relationship follows the selected verse.

hotspots.title: Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers
hotspots.note: The text names the brothers and identifies them as Jacob’s sons; the diagram shows the sibling relationship without the violent act.

hotspots.title: Jacob and his sons’ exchange
hotspots.note: The diagram marks the response and reply as a text relationship; it does not illustrate the retaliation.

scenes.title: Esau and his named family

art.alt: Native text diagram identifying Esau as Edom and showing named wives and sons with explicitly stated maternal links; not geography, chronology, or the full chapter.

scenes.caption: Diagram · Genesis 36:1–5 · selected family, not a map, timeline, or full chapter

intro.title: A selected family profile
intro.note: The diagram stops at the names in verses 1–5 and shows mother-child links only where stated. It does not extend the genealogy into later verses.

hotspots.title: Esau, who is Edom
hotspots.note: The name Edom is associated with Esau in the selected verse.

hotspots.title: Esau’s named wives
hotspots.note: The three named wives are shown with their references; the diagram does not invent additional family details.

hotspots.title: Sons through the named mothers
hotspots.note: The diagram connects Eliphaz, Reuel, and the sons of Aholibamah to the mothers named in the selected verses.
